newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila money market awaits T-bill auction.
newsitem.headline: Manila money market awaits T-bill auction.

text.p: Manila's secondary market for Treasury bills on Friday was lacklustre as financial institutions shied away to await the next auction of T-bills on Monday, traders said.
"Everybody is expecting rates in the next auction will go up. Instead of buying, they'd rather wait for the auction," a dealer said.

This resulted in slightly higher bid and offer rates for T-bills. A Reuters poll of eight financial institutions gave offers of 10.80/10.90 percent for the three-month bills; 11/11.25 percent for the six months; and 11.40/11.70 percent for the one year.
"Unless one sees a sign from the Central Bank it will bring down its rates, T-bill rates won't go down," a dealer said.
The Central Bank has maintained its 15 percent overnight borrowing rate for over a week now. It was forced to raise its rate again to protect the peso against the renewed weakness in the Thai baht.
Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson, however, said the monetary authority would like to see how T-bill rates would fare on Monday before considering adjusting its key rate.
The average interbank call loan rate stayed at an average of 15.03125 percent.
Volume rose to 18.16 billion pesos from 17.53 billion pesos.
The market had 34 lenders and 18 borrowers.
